great.name: Built-in Additional Sum Insured buffer (after base SI exhausted) — Accidental Hospitalization (optional cover)
great.quote: “Additional Sum Insured for Accidental Hospitalization' shall be utilized only after the Sum Insured has been completely exhausted;”
great.reference: Optional Cover 11: Additional Sum Insured for Accidental Hospitalization (Clause 3.11)
great.explanation: This creates an extra Sum Insured layer that activates after your base Sum Insured is exhausted (for accidental hospitalization, if you opt for this cover).

good.name: Initial waiting period
good.quote: “First 30-Day waiting Period… Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident”
good.explanation: 30-day initial waiting is standard in health insurance; accidents are covered immediately.

good.name: Specific illness waiting period
good.quote: “Specific Waiting Period… excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage”
good.explanation: 24 months for listed diseases/procedures is industry standard.

good.name: Pre-existing disease (PED) waiting period
good.quote: “Pre-existing Disease… shall be excluded until the expiry of 48 months of continuous coverage”
good.explanation: 48 months (4 years) for PED is within standard range (not a red flag).

good.name: Restore/Recharge benefit (unrelated illness only)
good.quote: “Automatic Recharge… re-instatement of up to the Sum Insured once in a policy year… The Recharge shall be available only for all future Claims which are not in relation to any Illness or Injury for which a Claim has already been admitted”
good.explanation: Restores up to 100% once in a policy year, but only for unrelated conditions (not the same illness).

good.name: Pre-hospitalization cover
good.quote: “Relevant Pre-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 30 days immediately prior”

good.name: Post-hospitalization cover
good.quote: “Relevant Post-hospitalization Medical Expenses, for a period of 60 days immediately after”

bad.name: Room rent / room category limit (default) + proportionate deduction applies
bad.quote: “If the Policy Schedule states ‘Single Private Room’ as eligible Room Category… payable by the Company is limited to stay in a Single Private Room.”
bad.explanation: Default room eligibility is capped to Single Private Room. If you take a higher room category, proportionate (ratable) deductions can apply on multiple hospital expenses.

bad.name: Mandatory co-pay for age 61+ (20% per claim) shown as applicable across plans
bad.quote: “Co-payment – 20% per claim, where age of insured / eldest member is 61 years or above”
bad.reference: Customer Information Sheet / KFD table (Clause 2(g) referenced)
bad.explanation: A mandatory 20% co-pay for seniors (61+) increases out-of-pocket on every claim, if this is applied by default as indicated in the plan table.

bad.name: Disease / procedure sub-limits (if enabled in policy schedule — shown for some plans)
bad.quote: “Expenses incurred on treatment for Named Ailments / Procedures… up to the amount specified against each… in the Policy Schedule… (These conditions will apply only if specifically mentioned in the Policy Schedule)”
bad.explanation: If your plan/policy schedule has these sub-limits turned on (e.g., cataract, knee replacement, hernia etc.), payouts can be capped per procedure, which can cause significant out-of-pocket.

bad.name: Consumables / non-medical items not covered
bad.quote: “Any item or condition or treatment specified in List of Non-Medical Items (Annexure – II to Policy Terms & Conditions).”
bad.explanation: Consumables and many common hospital items (e.g., gloves, masks, syringes, kits etc. listed in Annexure II) are excluded, increasing out-of-pocket costs.

bad.name: NCB reduces on claim (resets downward)
bad.quote: “In the event of a Claim occurring during any Policy Year, the accrued No Claims Bonus will be reduced by 10% of the Sum Insured at the commencement of next Policy Year”
bad.explanation: NCB is not protected; it reduces after a claim (many better policies protect bonus fully).

bad.name: Global Coverage (excluding USA) has mandatory 10% co-pay
bad.quote: “A mandatory Co-Payment of 10% per Claim is applicable, which will be in addition to any other co-payment (if any) applicable in the Policy.”
bad.explanation: If you use this benefit, you must pay 10% of each claim amount (over and above any other co-pay), reducing effective coverage.

unclear.name: Co-pay applicability: optional vs mandatory for age 61+ (conflicting signals between clauses/table)
unclear.quote: “If age of Insured Person or eldest Insured Person (in case of Floater) is 61 years or more, the Company provides an option… to choose for co-payment option of 20% per claim… and thereby get a discount of 20% in Premium” AND “Co-payment – 20% per claim, where age of insured / eldest member is 61 years or above”
unclear.reference: General Conditions 2 / Clause 2(g)(I) AND KFD loss sharing table (Clause 2(g))
unclear.explanation: One place says 20% co-pay for 61+ is optional (with premium discount), while the plan table suggests it applies for 61+ by default. Confirm in your policy schedule whether senior co-pay is mandatory or only if you opt for the discount.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
